abstract.t: This memo profiles the two-round threshold Schnorr signature scheme of RFC 9591 for the custody of the signing key of an organisational identity. No single member or device of the organisation ever holds that key, and a quorum of the organisation's authorised members signs on its behalf. The profile requires the FROST(Ed25519, SHA-512) ciphersuite. Because that ciphersuite produces ordinary Ed25519 signatures, a key held this way is published, rotated and verified exactly as the DNS-based discovery memo "Discovery of Model Context Protocol Servers via DNS TXT Records" already specifies, and no verifier needs to change. The memo specifies a distributed key- generation ceremony in which the whole key never exists in one place, the record of who may sign and how many must agree, the request and assembly of a signature, a signed custody statement by which a verifier learns that a published key is held under a threshold, and the handling of member removal, share refresh and loss. The memo is Informational.
